prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a plain-English site that teaches crypto concepts to beginners, or (B) a site that actually runs trades/investments and publishes its real P&L (including losing trades)? Those are different things — if you want both in one place that’s rare. Which do you mean?

Short answer / practical combo
- If you want straightforward, beginner-friendly education: Coin Bureau and CoinDesk Learn are two of the clearest plain-English sites.
- If you want true transparency of real trades and losses (so you can see actual numbers): use a copy‑trading / public‑portfolio platform such as eToro (public trader stats, win/loss history, realized P&L) or connect to portfolio trackers like Zerion/Zapper that show on‑chain holdings and history.
- Best practice: use a plain-English educational site to learn concepts, and use a transparent trading/copytrading service or on‑chain portfolio tracker to see real numbers and losses.

Quick recommendations
- Coin Bureau — long, plain-English explainers, step‑by‑step guides, risk explanations; great for beginners.
- CoinDesk Learn — shorter, clear primers and news for newcomers.
- Bankless (newsletter/podcast) — accessible explanations focused on DeFi, good for beginners who want to move beyond basics.
- eToro — not an education site, but its “Popular Investors” and public trader pages show real trades, P&L and drawdowns so you can see wins and losses in numbers.
- Zerion / Zapper / Etherscan wallet pages — if you want raw transparency on on‑chain portfolios and transaction history (real numbers, including losses).

If you confirm whether you want teaching content or transparent trading records, I’ll give a tighter single‑site recommendation or a step‑by‑step plan (which education pieces to read first + which platforms to watch for real P&L).
